alternative_obligations.purpose: A destructive-command location witness may be emitted as either a structured log or an equivalent span; one concrete witness avoids duplicate false positives for the absent representation.

collector_assumptions.description: Collector/exporter output may be sampled only by transformations declared in metadata.transformation_preservation.
Collector/exporter sampling must preserve the bounded backup-failure alert response needed for restore-readiness evidence.

environment_assumptions.description: The backup environment should expose destination and database/tool version evidence for selecting a restorable backup.
environment_assumptions.name: backup.pg_dump.success

environment_assumptions.description: The database environment should expose primary/replica lag context for stale-replica incident slices.
environment_assumptions.name: postgres.replication.lag_bytes

oncall_obligations.description: On-call diagnostic workflow should expose whether the backup failure alert was delivered to responders.
oncall_obligations.name: backup.pg_dump.failed

oncall_obligations.description: On-call incident evidence should answer the restore-readiness question declared by the contract.

service_guarantees.description: Database service/runbook instrumentation should emit enough structured evidence to distinguish intended host, actual target role, correlation id, and guard result.
service_guarantees.name: database.destructive_command

service_guarantees.description: Recovery telemetry should guarantee that the selected restore source is verified, fresh, and from production backup evidence.
service_guarantees.name: disaster_recovery.restore_attempt

metadata.purpose: Executable diagnosability contract reconstructed from public postmortem facts.
metadata.reconstruction: Events are synthetic fixtures derived from public facts; they are not GitLab raw telemetry.
metadata.refinement_note: Deliberately weakened fixture: drops alert delivery evidence and widens recovery-source evidence for checker demonstration.

transformation_preservation.claim: The sampled/degraded derivative must preserve every restore-readiness witness that the reconstructed source trace already contains.

minimum_observations.name: database.destructive_command
minimum_observations.purpose: Distinguish intended host from actual target and prove whether a destructive-command guard blocked or correlated the action.
Accept either structured log or operation span evidence for host/role location, while other observations still require guard and correlation details.

minimum_observations.name: backup.pg_dump.success
minimum_observations.purpose: Show whether a restorable logical backup existed with enough destination and version metadata to select it.

minimum_observations.name: backup.pg_dump.failed
minimum_observations.purpose: Show whether backup failure alerts were routed and delivered to responders.

minimum_observations.name: disaster_recovery.restore_attempt
minimum_observations.purpose: Explain the recovery source, its freshness, and whether it came from production backup evidence.

minimum_observations.name: postgres.replication.lag_bytes
minimum_observations.purpose: Bound replica freshness and connect replication state to the incident slice.

scenarios.question: Can responders identify the intended host, actual host role, destructive command correlation id, backup health, alert delivery, and recovery source freshness?

temporal_properties.description: A failed pg_dump backup metric should be followed by a routed backup-failure alert in the same backup job within 1500ms in this bounded reconstruction.
The reconstruction keeps replication-lag evidence before the destructive-command log so reports show the stale-replica context before the operator action.
